items.summary: The Iran SNSC opens Thursday morning Day 14 of contested compliance without a formal announcement — the thirteenth consecutive overnight period without a determination. The operative structural development is the Doha Qatar engagement: Iran fulfilled its commitment to meet Qatari mediators on July 1, and Iran Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi is expected to confirm working groups formed for MOU implementation follow-up. This is the first Iranian diplomatic movement on MOU implementation beyond the Swiss technical framework track, establishing a dual-track diplomatic architecture — Doha (MOU implementation follow-up) and Swiss (final-status nuclear access, enrichment levels, HEU stockpile disposition). The SNSC's continued silence is now analytically ambiguous in a positive direction: the Doha engagement suggests Iranian willingness to operationalize MOU implementation even without a formal SNSC re-closure retraction, potentially indicating the SNSC silence reflects deliberation rather than resistance. The physical Hormuz traffic build continues through the CENTCOM escort corridor; Kpler AIS data reflects sustained vessel movement advancing from the June 24 +105% day-over-day baseline. Approximately 80 mines remain in the central channel, constraining all transit to escorted routes. Lloyd's war-risk premiums hold at 3-8% of vessel value versus 0.25% pre-conflict. The Lloyd's normalization gate remains formally closed — a formal SNSC position change is the upstream requirement for the 118-tanker backlog's full commercial release and has not been issued. WTI crude is estimated in the approximately $65-68 range Thursday morning — Day 12 below the $74 normalization-confidence floor — declining from the $69-70 equilibrium that held through Wednesday. The decline reflects growing market confidence in the physical reopening as Doha engagement confirms diplomatic momentum; Lebanon risk premium from Hezbollah's Day 4 non-compliance provides a partial upward offset. The 60-day oil sanctions waiver (Day 15, through approximately August 18) provides approximately 46 days of structural time buffer. Oregon pump prices approximately $5.10-5.20/gallon; national approximately $4.40-4.48/gallon. Lebanon advances to approximately Hour ~220+ through Thursday morning. Hezbollah's 'null and void' rejection of the Rubio framework (Naim Qassem, June 28) is Day 4 morning — four consecutive overnight periods without military escalation following political non-compliance. This advancing durability signal continues to support the analytic read that the characterization is political positioning rather than operational prelude. IDF drone activity in southern Lebanon's 570 km² buffer zone continues Wednesday into Thursday; the buffer zone remains under Israeli presence. Netanyahu's 'as long as necessary' buffer posture unchanged. The IMO 118-tanker convoy framework remains paused since Day 5 post-IRGC cargo ship strike (June 26).

items.summary: Ukraine executed two additional refinery strikes June 28, extending the long-range economic warfare campaign against Russian oil infrastructure that has already produced the broadest domestic fuel disruption in Russia's conflict period. Russian fuel shortages are now operative across 55 of 83 federal entities — more than two-thirds of the country — with mandatory or private company fuel restrictions active simultaneously. The Kapotnya refinery, the largest fuel supplier to the Moscow metropolitan region, was struck twice this month and is tracking offline through at least year-end — the longest confirmed repair timeline of any struck facility. Crimea has escalated fuel restrictions to reserve gasoline and diesel for military and state use only, compounding the peninsula's geographic isolation from mainland distribution chains. An International Energy Agency assessment is expected imminently — current reporting characterizes the disruption scale as representing a validated strategic milestone for Ukrainian economic warfare with no precedent in the conflict's history. The military logistics implications for front-line fuel chains in Zaporizhzhia and Kupyansk corridors — which share distribution networks with the disrupted domestic system — are the primary emerging analog to watch. Putin publicly acknowledged the shortages — an extraordinary admission for Russian state media — while negotiations to import gasoline from Kazakhstan have been confirmed. Russia's ballistic missile production (74/month in 2026) and guided glide bomb program (75,000+ projected for 2026) continue as the parallel offensive posture backdrop. Peru ONPE closes cleanly: Keiko Fujimori has been declared winner. With approximately 50,000 more votes than Roberto Sánchez per the JNE tabulation of all ballots counted — a tight 50.10%/49.90% working count through 27 days — Fujimori will become Peru's first elected female president. JNE formal presidential declaration is expected tomorrow July 3. International election monitors confirmed no evidence of fraud. Sánchez has not conceded; the thread is closing regardless. North Korea Choe Hyon destroyer advances to Day 9 without new provocations — nuclear navy program ongoing. PRC 46-company ban Day 5; Chinese Coast Guard east-of-Taiwan patrol Day 33. Acting DNI Day 43 enters the ninth week without Senate-confirmed IC leadership.

items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics released the June employment situation at 8:30 AM ET Thursday morning — the week's primary market-moving event and the first of two primary inputs before the July 29 FOMC decision (June CPI July 14 is the second). The consensus expectation entering the report was approximately +113,000 nonfarm payrolls, a deceleration from May's +172,000 and substantially below the three-month average of approximately 188,000. The June print against that consensus is the FOMC October 2026 rate hike probability pivot: a strong print sustains or extends October hike market pricing; a miss repricies the probability downward. Chair Warsh's hawkish posture — nine hike-dots on the June dot plot, October hike market-priced, May PCE at 4.1% and May CPI at 4.2% — remains operative. The jobs report is also the primary demand signal input for WTI pricing at the current Hormuz equilibrium level: a jobs miss that signals demand cooling would add supply-side pressure to the already-declining WTI trajectory; a strong print reaffirms demand. US financial markets enter Thursday with two sequential structural catalysts in the pre-July 4 holiday window: the jobs report (today, primary macro catalyst) and SpaceX Nasdaq-100 entry (Sunday July 6, primary structural equity catalyst). WTI crude is estimated in the approximately $65-68 range Thursday morning — declining from the $69-70 equilibrium that held through Wednesday — as the Doha Iran diplomatic engagement and continued physical Hormuz traffic build increasingly price a formal reopening scenario. The $65-70 range is revising toward a pre-war floor estimate of approximately $63-67 as the most probable resolution scenario equilibrium absent re-escalation. SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 entry Sunday July 6 requires forced passive fund rebalancing at scale: Invesco QQQ ($490 billion) is adjusting; estimated passive buying in the $8-12 billion range; SpaceX's $2.5 trillion effective index weight with the Nasdaq's 3x multiplier accommodation creates displaced selling in members removed or reduced to make room. Pre-event capital positioning is active through Thursday and Friday — last two trading days before Sunday effective date. FOMC next decision July 29. The jobs report (today) and June CPI (July 14) are the two primary inputs remaining before that meeting.

items.summary: The Section 122 blanket 10% tariff on the vast majority of imported goods — imposed February 24, 2026 under Proclamation 11012 — reaches its statutory expiration on July 24, 2026 (12:01 AM EDT), now 22 days away. The Court of International Trade invalidated the tariff May 7 in a divided three-judge ruling (Oregon v. United States; Burlap and Barrel, Inc. v. United States), but the CAFC's administrative stay suspends the CIT injunction, keeping CBP collection active as of Thursday morning. The July 24 expiration is statutory and cannot be extended by executive action; congressional extension is considered unlikely given the legislative calendar and floor dynamics. The administration has confirmed plans to use the 150-day bridge as the foundation for longer-lasting authorities via Section 301 and Section 232 investigations, which carry no 150-day cap. Importers have a 22-day planning window for the tariff's statutory lapse — the most important trade policy transition since the initial February 24 imposition. OBBB enters Day 2 with all major provisions effective: Medicaid work requirements and per-capita block grant conversion, SALT modification, top individual rate reduction (retroactive to January 1, 2026), border security appropriations release, and IRA energy incentive phase-outs. CMS guidance on enforcement grace periods or waiver application frameworks for complex-population states (Oregon approximately 1.4 million enrollees; Washington approximately 2.2 million) remains the primary domestic unresolved implementation mechanism. FERC large-load show-cause orders advance to Day 16 — T-14 to the approximately July 18 response deadline for AI data center operators to explain their grid integration pathway. Final two weeks of the response window. USTR de minimis proposed rules comment period closes July 6 (this Sunday) with public hearing July 7. Section 232 (50% steel, aluminum, copper) advances to Day 31.

items.summary: The Tucannon Fire in southeastern Washington enters Day 5 Thursday morning with an overnight growth estimate in the approximately 20,000-25,000+ acre range — continuing advance from the ~20,000+ overnight estimate reported at Wednesday morning, driven by the second PNW heat wave's Day 2 arrival intensifying the already-record 100-hour fuel dryness environment (Northwest Coordination Center). Level 3 (Go Now) evacuation orders in Garfield County's Pomeroy area corridor remain active through Thursday morning. The second heat wave — arriving Wednesday and intensifying Thursday — is the Tucannon Fire's most significant near-term compound risk factor: the additional fuel dryness loading on an environment already described as record-setting for this calendar date extends Red Flag conditions toward the July 4 holiday weekend, now only two days away. The July 4 weekend represents the brief cycle's peak compound-ignition-risk convergence: maximum human ignition risk (fireworks, agricultural activity, holiday recreation) overlaid on record fuel dryness and active heat wave, four days before the July 7 FIFA PNW venue close — the window when recreational activity and public gatherings compound ignition probability across the East Cascades. Tule Road (Toppenish/Yakima County, approximately 24,087 acres) approaching final containment — resource release expected Thursday morning, providing partial suppression resource relief. Juniper Dunes near-containment. Garred Road (approximately 500 acres, 0% containment as of Wednesday evening) advancing to Day 3 as a potential additional ignition in Grant County. The Hamilton Fire (Winthrop/Okanogan County) advances to Day 2 active suppression: the overnight Day 1 partial stabilization held through Wednesday evening, with no new overnight expansion triggering additional evacuation orders beyond the full-Winthrop evacuation that was called and then partially de-escalated. The fire remains active and not fully contained, constituting the East Cascades onset period's second geographic suppression commitment — dual-front resource deployment between Tucannon (primary) and Hamilton/Winthrop (secondary) is now the operational baseline entering the primary July-September fire risk season with resources at active draw. NIFC Preparedness Level 3 advances to Day 16. BPA grid stable. NSF Newport OR operational.

items.summary: Oregon's renewable energy construction deadline is two days away — Friday July 4 is the federal tax credit qualification deadline for solar and wind projects to begin construction and retain 30-50% upfront cost credit (commercial service required by December 2027). Today (Thursday July 3) and tomorrow (Friday July 4, a federal holiday) are the literal closing days of the qualification window, but permitting offices and state agency siting functions are closed July 4 — making Thursday the last effective business day for projects in final permitting and construction-start documentation stages. Oregon Governor Kotek's Executive Order 25-25 (siting acceleration) has enabled mobilization of projects that would otherwise face multi-month permitting delays; the EO has been the enabling mechanism for projects attempting the late-stage qualification sprint. The financial consequence for projects that miss the construction-start documentation threshold is the loss of the 30-50% upfront tax credit — a cost differential that in many cases determines project viability. Thursday is the day with the highest permitting and construction-start filing volume of the entire Oregon renewable energy season. Washington Governor Ferguson's SB 6355 (Washington Electric Transmission Authority) enters Day 2 with its first planning mandate active; the Northwest Power Council expects to release its draft 20-year power plan for public comment this month — a significant planning document for PNW grid capacity that carries the new utility landscape (PGE/PacifiCorp integration) and WA Electric Transmission Authority mandate as its baseline inputs. Portland General Electric's acquisition of approximately 140,000 PacifiCorp Washington retail electricity customers (~$1.9 billion) is Day 2 with rate transition active. CISA CI Fortify: the IRGC cyber elevated actor posture enters Day 7 — now running parallel to the Doha engagement confirmation, which provides slightly more geopolitical context but does not reduce the threat window (the MOU's most permissive compliance window is structurally defined by the SNSC silence, not by diplomatic movement). items.summary: The Pacific Northwest opens Thursday July 2 morning with the wildfire-heat compound risk advancing into its most dangerous phase of the onset season. The Tucannon Fire has grown to an estimated 20,000-25,000+ acres overnight — continuing advance driven by the second PNW heat wave's Day 2 intensification of already record-setting 100-hour fuel dryness (Northwest Coordination Center). Level 3 evacuation orders in Garfield County's Pomeroy area corridor remain active. The second heat wave is arriving at its most intense phase Thursday — AccuWeather and NWS Spokane project record-challenging afternoon temperatures in the eastern fire zones; the compound fuel dryness and heat environment extends Red Flag conditions directly into the July 4 holiday weekend, now only two days away. The July 4 weekend represents the brief cycle's single most elevated compound-ignition-risk window: the intersection of peak heat and fuel dryness with maximum regional human ignition risk (fireworks, agricultural activity, holiday recreation) during the onset of the primary July-September wildfire season. Fireworks safety is a particular concern given the record fuel environment — consumer and professional fireworks ignitions in adjacent or downwind fuels are the primary human-ignition risk category entering the holiday weekend. The Hamilton Fire (Winthrop/Okanogan County) enters Day 2 with a partial positive: Day 1's overnight new-ignition partial stabilization held through Wednesday evening without re-expansion triggering new evacuations. The fire remains active and not fully contained, constituting the East Cascades onset season's second geographic suppression commitment. Resources are split between Tucannon (primary, 20,000+ acres) and Hamilton/Winthrop (secondary, stabilizing but active). Tule Road (Toppenish/Yakima, ~24,087 acres) near final containment — resource release expected this morning provides partial relief. Oregon Coast M5.5 earthquake (struck approximately 4:35 AM Monday) — no damage reported, no tsunami; the Cascadia Subduction Zone seismic hazard backdrop remains the structural long-horizon risk. The Historic Columbia River Highway landslide east of Corbett enters Day 3 with all lanes closed (ODOT) — active transportation infrastructure disruption in the Columbia River Gorge affecting tourist and freight routes. Lake Chelan closed to boaters — 2024 Pioneer Fire burn scar runoff continues to deliver logs, ash, and sediment; the closure is disrupting the lake's summer recreational economy at peak season. NIFC PL3 Day 16. BPA grid stable.
